stage_a.note: Constant smiling, enthusiastic vocal tone, and large joyful gestures throughout.
Highly animated delivery expressing great excitement about the gnomes and the business.
Very friendly and approachable, placing hands on heart and expressing gratitude.

venture.description: Decorative plush gnomes for the home, including pre-made designs for various occasions and a custom design-a-gnome option.
venture.note: The ask is clearly stated at the beginning of the pitch.

turns.summary: Wendy explains Barbara was chosen to experience the custom design process.

turns.summary: Barbara jokes about having to work for her gnome.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Wendy says she gets to pick it out herself.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Barbara expresses approval.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Wendy explains they are used around the home to make people smile.

turns.summary: Wendy starts the custom design process with Barbara.

turns.summary: Barbara selects a sunflower embellishment.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Wendy asks for the hat color and boots.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Wendy says it will take a few minutes to build.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Wendy states that sales come from their website and Etsy.

turns.speaker: S5

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Wendy states her customer acquisition cost is about five dollars.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Wendy says the average price is thirty-five dollars.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Wendy states it costs three dollars and fifty cents for materials.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark is impressed by the margins.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Kevin asks if there are cheaper gnome options available.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Wendy says her prices are comparable to others on Etsy.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark asks if people brush their gnomes.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Wendy confirms they tell people to comb their gnomes.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark jokes that Kevin will finally have something to comb.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Kevin laughs at Mark's joke.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark expresses amazement that people pay thirty-five dollars for the product.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori asks to understand the gnome market better.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Wendy explains people have an emotional connection to gnomes.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori asks what her sales have been to date.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Wendy states she has made over six hundred thousand in eighteen months.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Daymond is shocked by the sales figures.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Barbara expresses disbelief at the sales.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori is amazed that the small items generate such sales.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Kevin assumes there must be many tall gnomes online.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Wendy explains she is the top seller on Etsy despite factory competition.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori is impressed by her top seller status.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Daymond asks how she started the hobby that became so successful.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Wendy shares that she started making gnomes after a bad breakup.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Kevin jokes that the broken heart turned into cash flow.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori calls Wendy the gnome goddess.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark asks about her initial investment and profitability.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Wendy states she started the business with less than one thousand dollars.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark calculates the massive return on her initial investment.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Wendy adds that they netted over one hundred thirty thousand last year.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Daymond praises her profitability.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Kevin asks how many people work in the business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Wendy says she employs three women and her daughter.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: The daughter presents Barbara's completed custom gnome.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Barbara loves the gnome and feels motherly toward it.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori asks about Wendy's professional background.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Wendy explains she was a labor and delivery nurse.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori asks the daughter how she feels about her mother's success.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: The daughter expresses immense pride and notes they both retired from nursing.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Kevin praises the story but exits because he doesn't need a gnome business.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori exits, stating it is a thriving business but not the right fit for her.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark exits, feeling it is too niche a category for him to invest in.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Daymond asks how an investor could add value to the business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Wendy explains she needs a strategic partner for marketing and SEO.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Daymond offers two hundred thousand for thirty-five percent equity.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Kevin jokes that the gnome's hair is falling off.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Daymond invites Wendy to counter his offer.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Barbara asks if gnomes have been popular for a long time.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Wendy confirms that gnomes have been around forever.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Barbara asks why the overhead is so high relative to sales.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Wendy explains that a lot of the expenses are Etsy fees.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Barbara offers two hundred thousand for thirty percent plus a royalty.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Kevin notes that Barbara is asking for a royalty.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Barbara clarifies she calls it a buck a gnome, not a royalty.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Daymond revises his offer to thirty percent plus a temporary royalty.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Barbara drops her royalty, offering a straight thirty percent equity deal.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Kevin points out that there is now a competition between the sharks.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori asks Wendy what she is going to do.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Wendy asks Daymond if he will match Barbara's offer.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Daymond asks if she means the exact same terms.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Barbara accuses Wendy of playing them against each other.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Daymond asks why they should keep negotiating against themselves.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Wendy asserts that the business is worth it and will be profitable.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Daymond asks for her projected revenue and net profit for the year.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Wendy projects seven hundred fifty thousand in revenue and one hundred fifty thousand net.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Daymond calculates his potential return based on her projections.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Daymond decides to match Barbara's offer of thirty percent for two hundred thousand.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Barbara criticizes Daymond, calling him rude.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Barbara pitches her expertise in moving businesses off outside websites.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Wendy counters both offers, asking for twenty-five percent equity instead.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Barbara refuses to lower her equity ask.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Daymond also refuses to lower his equity ask.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Kevin asks Wendy what her final decision will be.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Wendy accepts Daymond's offer.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Daymond celebrates the deal with Wendy.
